findings.answer: Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, multimodal, 64 layers of which only 16 are full-attention. bf16 is 51.8 GiB and does not fit.
findings.question: What is the architecture, and does bf16 fit 48 GiB?

findings.answer: Concurrency. KV is 64 KiB/token and only the 16 full-attention layers grow with it; the 48 Gated-DeltaNet layers cost ~78 MB per sequence regardless of length.
findings.question: Is context or concurrency the binding constraint?

findings.answer: Not by pip. vLLM >=0.20 defaults to CUDA 13, which needs driver >=580. A +cu129 release asset works but is not on PyPI. There is also an open CUDA-graph hang on exactly the RTX A5000.
findings.question: Can vLLM be installed on driver 535?

findings.answer: Only llama.cpp, which grammar-constrains it. vLLM and SGLang parse Qwen's XML after the fact from unconstrained output.
findings.question: Which stack guarantees a well-formed tool call?

unresolved: Whether 4-bit quantisation degrades tool-calling accuracy — no published data either way; WP-009 must measure it rather than inherit an assumption.
Whether upgrading to driver 580 to unlock vLLM's measured 85-95 tok/s is worth a host-wide change.
